routes.name: 45-day visa exemption (unilateral policy)
routes.summary: Citizens of 12 countries can enter Vietnam without a visa for up to 45 days, any passport type and any purpose. The policy runs from March 15, 2025 to March 14, 2028.

other: You still have to meet Vietnam's normal entry conditions.
Belarus is not in the 12-country list. Belarus ordinary passports get 30 days, with no more than 90 days in a calendar year, under the separate MOFA list.

stay.note: Counted from the date of entry. Policy valid March 15, 2025 to March 14, 2028.

sources.label: Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Viet Nam's visa exemption list

routes.name: Visa exemption for other listed countries (treaty and ASEAN)
routes.summary: Vietnam exempts citizens of about 96 countries under bilateral deals. Stays for ordinary passports run from 14 to 90 days depending on the country. Check the official MOFA list for your passport.

other: Ordinary passport examples from the MOFA list: Thailand, Malaysia, Laos, Cambodia, Singapore, Indonesia and Myanmar get 30 days. Brunei gets 14 days. The Philippines gets 21 days. Belarus, Kazakhstan get 30 days, capped at 90 days a year or per 180 days.
Many entries on the list apply only to diplomatic or official passports. Check the passport type column for your country.
British National (Overseas) passports are not exempt.
The Czech, Polish and Swiss 45-day tour exemption ended December 31, 2025.
The MOFA page is dated June 30, 2025. Confirm it is still current before relying on it.

routes.name: Phu Quoc island visa exemption
routes.summary: Foreign passport holders can enter or leave through Phu Quoc island without a visa for up to 30 days. This also works if you first pass through another Vietnamese international border gate.

other: Based on Decision 80/2020/QD-TTg, as listed on the MOFA page.

sources.label: Ministry of Foreign Affairs: Viet Nam's visa exemption list

routes.name: Vietnam eVisa
routes.summary: Citizens of all countries can apply online for an eVisa. It is valid up to 90 days, single or multiple entry, and works at listed airports, land border gates and seaports.

other: Open to all nationalities since August 15, 2023.
Run by the Immigration Department under the Ministry of Public Security. Embassy states e-visas are processed in Hanoi, not by the embassy.

The eVisa fee and processing time were not readable. The portal loads blank for automated reading. The 2026 fee circular lists regular visa fees of USD 25 single and USD 50 multiple under 90 days, but does not name the eVisa. Check evisa.gov.vn.

stay.note: Validity of up to 90 days. Single or multiple entry.

steps: Apply on the official eVisa portal run by the Immigration Department.
Pick your entry border gate from the approved list (13 airports, 16 land gates and 13 seaports per the embassy notice).

routes.name: Regular visa from an embassy
routes.summary: You can apply for a regular visa at a Vietnamese embassy or consulate. Work, study and conference visas need an approval letter from Vietnamese immigration or consular authorities first.

other: Passport valid at least 6 months past your planned departure.
Employment, study and conference visas need an approval letter from Vietnamese authorities.

steps: Apply online through the embassy consular portal or in person.
Submit the form, photos and passport.
Pay the fee and wait for the visa.
documents: Two passport photos on a light background
Approval letter (work, study or conference visas)
